title: an array literal of Results is consumed by reading an element back out with postfix !
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx §Configuration (the worked example this case is written from): '`arr[i]!` does not silently change meaning, and it compiles when `arr` holds Results. The `| undefined` an index read adds under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is not the author's — the option widens the *access*, never the container's element type — so it is seen through, and `arr[i]!` means there what `!` means everywhere else.' This is the specification's own worked example, written as a program. Building the array is not the discard: ownership moves to the container, and reading an element back out is where the obligation lands. REVIEW-fable-1.md F5 measured the reference REJECTING this exact shape with two SMITHERS1301 at the element positions while the Go fork accepted and ran it — a false rejection of the one spelling the specification promises compiles. The refusal direction is pinned by the two sibling cases below, so a fix that simply stopped charging array elements fails those. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-28 by running both backends with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` ON, which is when this case first had anything to say: it passed before only because the mandatory option was off. With the option on and the provenance walk unchanged, the reference refused it SMITHERS1207 'postfix ! requires a Result operand' — the specification's own example, refused by the option the specification mandates. The expectation is UNCHANGED at `output`; what changed is that it is now earned. The walk sees through the `| undefined` the ACCESS gained (the container's element type never gained one), and the lowering asserts it in the emitted TypeScript, without which the generated program failed the emit check at TS2345/TS18048. Both backends measured green.
